name: Bertolome Zorzi
bio: Bertolome Zorzi was a gentleman of Venice who, in the Life Farnell translates, was taken captive by the Genoese, who were at war with the Venetians.

The verse in this selection is Ida Farnell's English version in The Lives of the Troubadours (London: David Nutt, 1896), where it stands beside a prose Life of the poet; the prose Life is not reproduced here. The dates are those Farnell prints for the period in which the poet was active, and the Old Occitan original is not included.

poems.title: Prayer to the Virgin
poems.author: Bertolome Zorzi
poems.text:
Sancta Maria, all maidens exceeding,
God's own beloved, mankind to him leading,
Look down in pity, give ear to my pleading,
Mercy, sweet lady!

Mother, most holy — oh! do not disdain me,
God's gracious pardon I pray thee to gain me.
Fruit and eke fruit-tree of virtue, maintain me,
Mercy, sweet lady!

With thy sweet pity, I pray thee, befriend me,
Free me from evil, thy happiness send me,
And from Hell's torments I pray thee defend me,
Mercy, sweet lady!

Mother of Jesus, by doubt sore distressed,
May I have guidance of thee ever blessed,
Who God's high favour hast ever possessed,
Mercy, sweet lady!
